raw:
{
  "question_intent": "Assess the impact of AI on deposit spread compression, NII, and wealth market, and the reaction to NatWest Evelyn's acquisition.",
  "main_topics": [
    "AI impact on deposit market",
    "NII and technology",
    "AI in wealth market",
    "Market reaction to NatWest Evelyn"
  ],
  "answer_completeness": "Complete",
  "response_stance": "Direct",
  "evidence_level": "High",
  "contains_numeric_evidence": true,
  "contains_forward_guidance": false,
  "narrative_alignment": "Aligned",
  "question_quote": "What are the sort of the chances that, that level of deposit spread compression persists forever? And the NII actually comes out at £8.1 billion and flat lines because it's just expensive to run in the deposit market, and this just gets perpetually chipped away by technology. And then secondly, kind of on AI as well, just what impact you see it having in the wealth market, given that's a bit of a focus last week and kind of looking at the reaction that the market has had and investors had to NatWest Evelyn. Does that make you question the reaction that people have had, does that make you question any acquisitions in wealth now?",
  "answer_quote": "Thank you, Rob. Well, Vim Maru was reminding me yesterday that the first such platform was launched by Bradford and Bingley some time ago. So, this kind of approach has been out there for some time. We've obviously seen it become more sophisticated. But customers are moving their deposits around now. It's pretty much a friction-free market because we're nearly all optimising our deposits on our app, and it's pretty easy to do. That said, we are not seeing a significantly higher level of term deposits than we saw immediately post crisis. So there seems to be a sort of natural level, if you like. That said, we can't rely on that, which is why we're investing so much in the app because actually, what you want to do is bring your customers into your environment and for them to find everything that they need there so that they don't need to go. And obviously, that means that you know them better because you have the primary banking relationship, you can give them the kind of nudges that it's much more difficult to do on a sort of open banking basis. So we think that's the way to address this. Clearly, we are also assuming that deposit margin pressure does not ease. So that was back to the question from Ed. So we're not assuming that we find out of this by the end of the year and that there's any difference in the margin pressure in this business. You then need to think about what happens sort of if rates continue to go lower, then you make less and less money out of deposits anyway and you start to make more and more out of assets. That's why it's really important for NII longevity, that there is some diversification within NII. We're very, very focused as an industry, I guess, as a sort of investor group at the moment on the margins within deposits. But we have to grow NII from assets now because the rate cycle will tell you that in low rates, you make more in assets, less in deposits. That will come. And so for those challengers, that is quite a challenge to the model. You can't just be a deposit taker. You do what you do with those deposits? How are you going to lend them. So, we do think about it through the cycle, we do think about it on a more holistic basis and technology is really, really important, not only engaging the customer on the deposit side, but also ensuring that we are lending to them and deepening that relationship. In terms of wealth and AI, it depends on what you mean about wealth. So, there's a huge continuum here around how people think about their wealth and how they place it. So, if you go from our Private Banking business, -it's very high touch, very human-led. If you remember that slide that Venkat had, it was the one that's over on the left-hand side, and we would probably see that persisting. So, if you're looking at a Private Banking model, it's going to be predominantly human-led. If you're at the other end where you are an execution-only model like Smart Investor, now renamed Direct Investing, I think, that has to be execution only, completely digital, etc. Then wealth is somewhere in the middle. So, you are going to want to have your customers dealing with you digitally, getting digital prompts. And that's why that advice guidance boundary piece of work that the government is doing is so important because at the moment, the boundary to receiving advice is quite a high one. I give you advice, you pay me. That's what RDR requires. But actually, in advice guidance, it becomes a bit more like people like Rob, looks at things like this. So it's much more prompting guiding. In that kind of environment, you would expect AI to be much more relevant, the kind of nudges and understanding that you have of our customers. That's why we think this link between our 'Premier' and our 'Affluent' customers and that digital link from the app back to the point I made about you get in the app and you stay in that ecosystem and extending that all the way over into wealth, we think is really important. That does not exist in the UK at this point in time. That doesn't exist. So, you can come at it in a couple of ways. You can either buy a predominantly adviser-led wealth business and sort of try and push it right to left or you can go the other way. And obviously, that's what we're trying to do.",
  "main_topics": [
    "NII and technology",
    "AI in wealth market",
    "Market reaction to NatWest Evelyn"
  ],
  "answer_completeness": "Complete",
  "response_stance": "Direct",
  "evidence_level": "High",
  "contains_numeric_evidence": true,
  "contains_forward_guidance": false,
  "narrative_alignment": "Aligned",
  "contains_numeric_evidence": true,
  "contains_forward_guidance": false
}
